the anonymous clauses of the found-notes mishnah (12b.16)
the baraita of 13b.5-7, תניא כוותיה דרבי יוחנן

props.gloss_en: found notes bearing a property guarantee are not returned: the court would collect from encumbered property on their strength
R' Meir: notes without a property guarantee are returned, for the court does not collect from encumbered property on their strength
the Chachamim: either way the note is not returned
the mishnah's case (on the stam's first account): the debtor admits the debt
the concern: the note was written to borrow in Nisan but the loan happened only in Tishrei, and the holder would seize from buyers of the interim unlawfully
why suspect only these? ordinary notes are unimpaired; a note that FELL is impaired
the cited mishnah: a note may be written for the borrower even in the lender's absence -- inviting the predating concern from the outset
Rav Assi: the write-in-absence mishnah concerns deeds of transfer, where the writer obligated himself from the writing date -- so no predating harm
Rav Assi on our mishnah: a non-transfer note that fell is impaired -- perhaps it merely happened to be written and no loan followed

Abaye: the signing witnesses acquire for the holder from the writing date, even in non-transfer notes -- so no predating concern (he rejects Rav Assi's split: since non-transfer notes are not written in the lender's absence, accidental writing cannot arise)
the found-documents mishnah (the mishnah bm_18a's sugya expounds): such documents are not returned, lest they were written and the writer reconsidered
the deflection: the signatures acquire only where the document has already reached the owner's hand
Abaye's account of our mishnah: the found note is withheld because we suspect repayment, and collusion against the buyers
Shmuel's rule: we suspect neither repayment nor collusion
Shmuel reads the mishnah as a case where the debtor does NOT admit
(Shmuel's report of R' Meir) an unguaranteed note collects neither from encumbered nor from free assets
then why return it at all? R' Natan bar Oshaya: to cap the lender's flask -- the paper itself is his
and not the borrower's flask: the borrower has denied the matter ever happened
R' Elazar: the tannaitic dispute concerns only the case where the debtor does not admit
R' Elazar: where the debtor admits, all agree the note is returned -- neither repayment nor collusion is suspected
R' Yochanan: the dispute concerns only the case where the debtor admits
R' Yochanan: where the debtor does not admit, all agree it is not returned, for repayment is suspected
the baraita: a guaranteed note is returned to neither party even when both admit; and R' Meir's unguaranteed note collects from free assets

supports.gloss_en: תניא כוותיה דרבי יוחנן: the baraita withholds the guaranteed note even where both admit, and suspects collusion -- R' Yochanan's map of the dispute

challenges.gloss_en: תיובתא דרבי אלעזר בחדא -- the baraita keeps the guaranteed note from both parties even when both admit, so collusion IS suspected
תיובתא דשמואל (count one): the baraita suspects collusion where both admit
תיובתא דשמואל (count two): the baraita has R' Meir's unguaranteed note collecting from free assets, against Shmuel's report that it collects from neither
